clue.text: Best tempo not completely set in stone

indicators.note: a gem is set in a mount; here the shortened word is put inside the stone

parts.note: opal is a gemstone

indicators.note: the word for tempo loses its final letter, so it is not complete

parts.note: tempo can mean time, as in musical time

explanation.surface: Someone muses that the ideal pace for something is not fully fixed yet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set in stone' reads as the idiom for fixed, but here 'set in' and 'stone' do separate jobs, a gem mounted around the shortened word.
explanation.definitionFit: Optimal describes the most favourable choice, a straightforward synonym of best.

indicators.note: the worker's word comes after the word for leaving in the answer

parts.note: to be off is to be leaving or departing
a hand is a hired worker, as in farmhand

explanation.surface: A temporary member of staff is spotted just after quitting time.
explanation.definitionFit: An offhand manner is casual and unconcerned, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Tense worker, with odd display of temper

parts.note: T is the grammar abbreviation for tense
an ant is the classic crossword worker, from worker ants
rum is an old-fashioned British word for odd or strange

explanation.surface: A stressed employee behaves strangely and loses their cool.
explanation.definitionFit: A tantrum is an outburst of childish anger, a classic display of temper.

clue.text: One topping cleric? Main target regularly!

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals, here the first, third, fifth and so on of the two words

explanation.surface: An archery-style instruction to aim at the bull's-eye, oddly framed with talk of a clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topping' means sitting on top of: the definition is something worn on a bishop's head.
explanation.definitionFit: A mitre is the tall headdress a bishop wears, so it sits on top of a cleric.

clue.text: Poor clues about protagonist with roving eye?

indicators.note: the reshuffled letters go about, that is around, the hero
poor signals that the letters of clues are badly arranged and must be reworked

parts.note: the protagonist of a story is its hero

explanation.surface: A critic grumbles about weak hints concerning a womanising main character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with roving eye' describes a person given to ogling, so the adjective swaps cleanly into a sentence like 'a man with roving eye'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with a roving eye keeps looking lustfully at others, which is what lecherous means.

clue.text: Shown this, player has to go — one from Hearts?

definitions.text: Shown this, player has to go
definitions.meaning: first meaning: the card a referee shows to send a footballer off
second meaning: any playing card from the hearts suit is red

explanation.walkthrough: Hearts looks like the Edinburgh football club, keeping the surface in football; the second reading is a card from the hearts suit.
explanation.definitionFit: In football a dismissal is signalled with a red card, and a heart in a pack of playing cards is a red one too.

clue.text: Meal to go bad when being eaten?

indicators.note: the little word is being eaten, swallowed inside the word for decaying

parts.note: to rot is to go bad
as can mean when, as in 'as he arrived'

explanation.surface: A question about whether food spoils while someone is eating it.
explanation.definitionFit: A roast is a meal of roasted meat, such as the British Sunday dinner.

indicators.note: reckless signals letters thrown about carelessly, so the speed before it is rearranged

parts.note: speed is rate, as in going at a fast rate

explanation.surface: An alarmed shout at a driver going far too fast, repeated for emphasis.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated phrase does three jobs: the first 'Reckless' is the definition, the first 'speed' is rearranged by the second 'Reckless' into DESPE, and the last 'speed' gives RATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Desperate actions are rash ones taken without regard to danger, so it means reckless.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the Swedish pop group ABBA released an album with this title in 1976
second meaning: a coming, an act of reaching a place

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as news of a new record; the second definition is the noun 'coming'.
explanation.definitionFit: An arrival is the act of reaching a destination, the noun sense of coming, and it is also the name of an ABBA record.

indicators.note: the extremes of the word dodgy are its first and last letters

parts.note: nasty means disgusting

explanation.surface: Someone condemns a remark or queue as very shady and revolting.
explanation.definitionFit: A dynasty is a line of rulers from the same family, the genealogical sense of line.

clue.text: Zealot in cooler upstairs room losing heart

parts.note: a fan cools a room

indicators.note: the room's word drops one of its two middle letters, its heart

parts.note: an attic is a room at the top of a house

explanation.surface: A fanatic sits in a chilly loft that has lost its spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: A fanatic is someone with extreme, uncritical enthusiasm, close in sense to zealot.

parts.note: also means too, in addition
to run something is to organise it, so organised gives ran

explanation.surface: Something over-planned turns out to be a flop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organised' looks like an anagram signal, but it simply means RAN, as in ran the event.
explanation.definitionFit: An also-ran is a contestant who finished unplaced, hence an unsuccessful person.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: consistency, as between two accounts
second meaning: a contract between parties

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a legal document being consistent; both words separately define the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Agreement covers both accord between things that match and a formal deal between parties.

clue.text: Singer in swivel — wife going nuts

indicators.note: going says one letter leaves, and nuts says the rest are scrambled

explanation.surface: A singer famous for swivelling hips, with his wife driven mad.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove W from SWIVEL to leave SIVEL, then rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Elvis Presley was the famous rock'n'roll singer, known for his hip-swivelling moves.

clue.text: Spirit shown in March and November

parts.note: a protest march is a demo
N is November in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A ghost appears in two particular months of the year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'March' and 'November' look like calendar months, but March is a protest and November a radio letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A demon is an evil supernatural being, one kind of spirit.

parts.note: nigh means near

indicators.note: the numeral is packed inside the word for bath

parts.note: a bath is a tub
CL is 150 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A place close to the English city of Bath crams in 150 people.
explanation.walkthrough: Bath looks like the English city; here it is a tub.
explanation.definitionFit: A spot is informal for a venue, especially a nightclub, as in a hot spot.

parts.note: old means former, as in an old flame
David Bailey is a celebrated British fashion photographer

explanation.surface: A one-time photographer is linked with a famous law court.
explanation.definitionFit: The Old Bailey is the popular name for London's Central Criminal Court.

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters are mixed together

explanation.surface: A morbid longing linked to the underworld god Hades.
explanation.definitionFit: A death wish is a conscious or unconscious longing to die, a dark yearning indeed.

clue.text: Most of East Anglia redeveloped — effect of numbers?

indicators.note: redeveloped, like a site rebuilt, means the letters are rebuilt into a new order
most of the word East is all but its last letter

explanation.surface: Much of eastern England is rebuilt, perhaps through statistics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'numbers' is not figures but things that numb: anaesthetics.
explanation.definitionFit: Analgesia is the loss of pain sensation, the result of a numbing drug.

parts.note: august means imposing or majestic

explanation.surface: A grand district in a city of Georgian architecture.
explanation.walkthrough: Georgian suggests eighteenth-century British style; here it means the US state of Georgia.
explanation.definitionFit: Augusta is a city in the US state of Georgia, home of the Masters golf tournament.

indicators.note: the remaining letters are distributed afresh in a new order
without its end, so the final letter of magazine goes

explanation.surface: A wonderful periodical is handed out again without end.
explanation.definitionFit: Amazing and fantastic are both informal words of high praise, meaning wonderful.

clue.text: Bounder dying to tour Californian city

indicators.note: the word for death travels around the city

parts.note: end can mean death, the act of dying
LA is Los Angeles

explanation.surface: A cad on his last legs takes a trip around Los Angeles.
explanation.walkthrough: A bounder is old British slang for a cad; here it is something that bounds.
explanation.definitionFit: The eland is a large African antelope, an animal that leaps, so a literal jumper.

indicators.note: peeled removes the outer letters of Dave, its skin

parts.note: Ocado is a British online grocery retailer

explanation.surface: A man named Dave strips a piece of fruit bought from a delivery grocer.
explanation.definitionFit: The avocado is the pear-shaped green fruit of a tropical tree.

clue.text: Faulty info about love causes resentment

parts.note: a dud is something faulty

indicators.note: the word for information goes about the zero

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
love is zero in tennis, hence O

explanation.surface: Bad information concerning a romance breeds bitterness.
explanation.definitionFit: Dudgeon is a feeling of offence or indignation, as in 'in high dudgeon'.

indicators.note: the Scotsman's name goes in, inside the car's initials

parts.note: GT stands for gran turismo, a kind of sports car
Ian is a typical Scottish name

explanation.surface: A huge Scot squeezes into a sports car.
explanation.definitionFit: Giant as an adjective means huge, the same as enormous.

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of ignores

parts.note: Sherwood is the forest near Nottingham, home of Robin Hood

explanation.surface: An author at first takes no notice of a football club.
explanation.walkthrough: Nottingham Forest is an English football club; here it is the actual forest.
explanation.definitionFit: Christopher Isherwood was an English novelist, author of Goodbye to Berlin.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in the NATO phonetic alphabet the letter I is spoken as this word
second meaning: the large South Asian nation

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a diplomat speaking for a nation; 'I' is the letter, not the speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: India is both a South Asian nation and the radio code word for the letter I.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the radio acknowledgement for message received
second meaning: the first name of the Swiss tennis player

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a fan calling to the tennis star; both halves define the answer separately.
explanation.definitionFit: Roger is radio procedure for message understood, and the given name of the tennis champion Federer.

indicators.note: the word for slipped sits outside the word for child

parts.note: slid means slipped
a kid is a child

explanation.surface: A youngster slipped over outdoors, so protective headgear was required.
explanation.definitionFit: A skid lid is British slang for a motorcycle crash helmet.

clue.text: Sort unlikely to appreciate popular grid

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable
a grate is a grid of bars, as in a fireplace

explanation.surface: Someone is unlikely to admire a well-liked crossword grid.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingrate is an ungrateful person, the type who fails to show thanks.

indicators.note: tortured means twisted, so the film star's name is twisted into a new order

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: It reads like a film title about Clark Gable as a tormented painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Algebra is a school subject, a branch of mathematics.

clue.text: Marx Brother talking about whaler's weapon

parts.note: Harpo was one of the Marx Brothers, the comedy team
on means about, as in talking on a subject

explanation.surface: A Marx Brother discusses a whaling weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that Harpo was the silent Marx Brother.
explanation.definitionFit: A harpoon is the barbed spear thrown or fired at whales.
